core_obligations: Verify flatness and quasi-compactness (proof lines 5152-5154): the projection p : S_K -> S is the base change of Spec(K) -> Spec(k), hence flat and quasi-compact.

Verify connectedness of the geometric fibres (proof lines 5154-5157): the fibre of p over a geometric point Spec(L) -> S is the spectrum of K tensor over k L, which is irreducible and therefore connected by the Algebra lemma invoked, k being separably algebraically closed.
Conclude (proof line 5152): the hypotheses of the companion sections-upstairs result are satisfied, giving the displayed equality of section sets.
proof_roadmap: Recall the companion result comparing sections of a sheaf with sections of its pullback under a flat quasi-compact base change with connected geometric fibres.
Check flatness and quasi-compactness of the projection from the base change construction.
Check that every geometric fibre is connected, using irreducibility of the tensor product over a separably closed field.
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a field extension K/k with k separably algebraically closed and a scheme S over k, the sections over S of a sheaf on S_etale agree with the sections over S_K of its pullback (statement lines 5142-5149). The proof is a complete verification of the hypotheses of the companion result on sections upstairs: flatness and quasi-compactness of the projection are read off from the base change description (proof lines 5152-5154), and the connectedness of the geometric fibres is reduced to irreducibility of K tensor over k L for a geometric point with residue field L, which is the Algebra lemma invoked (proof lines 5154-5157). The non-formal content is the two hypothesis verifications. The claim is H2: a reduction whose inputs are named and checked.
